unit.unitTitle: Your Home and the Rooms in It

cefr.bandName: Pre-A1, from no English at all

unit.unitOverview:
Say where you live.
Name the rooms in a home.
Say what there is in each room.
Say my home and our home.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: home and rooms.
Patterns: I live in, and there is a kitchen.
Listen to three short texts.
Describe your home. Record it.
Write four lines about where you live.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Name the rooms in a home
Say what there is in a room
Ask a person where they live
Say my and our about a place
Say a place is clean or not
unit.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 12. Where do you live?
First, two words. House and flat.
A house is a whole building.
A flat is part of a building.
And home is where you live, house or flat.
Say them with me. House. Flat. Home.
Now, I live in.
I live in a flat.
I live in a small house.
Say it with me. I live in.
Now the rooms.
The kitchen. You cook there.
The bedroom. You sleep there.
The bathroom. You wash there.
And the toilet.
Say them with me. Kitchen. Bedroom. Bathroom. Toilet.
Some homes have a garden. Some have stairs.
Now we use a pattern from Unit 8.
There is a kitchen.
There are two bedrooms.
Remember: one thing is, more than one are.
Last, my and our.
I live alone: my flat.
I live with people: our flat.
Say them with me. My flat. Our flat.
That is Unit 12. Go and describe your home.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: I live in
grammar.explanation:
Two small words say where your home is.
Live always takes in for a place.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I live in a flat.
I live in a small house.
I live in London.

he, she, it → lives
She lives in a house.

Question: Where do you live?
grammar.workedExample:
Your home is a flat.
1. Start: I live.
2. Then in.
3. Then a flat.
4. Say: I live in a flat.
5. Add more: I live in a small flat.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I live a flat.
English needs in.
Yes: I live in a flat.
grammar.memoryTip: Live takes in for a place.
grammar.practice:
Finish each one.
1. I ___ ___ a flat.
2. She ___ ___ a house.
3. Where do you ___?
4. They ___ ___ a big house.
grammar.answerKey:
1. live in
2. lives in
3. live
4. live in
All four? She and he take lives, with an s.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: There is a kitchen
grammar.explanation:
This is the pattern from Unit 8, on new ground.
One room: there is. More rooms: there are.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
There is a kitchen.
There are two bedrooms.
There is a garden.
There are no stairs.

Question: Is there a garden?
          Are there two bedrooms?
grammar.workedExample:
Your flat has one kitchen and two bedrooms.
1. One kitchen, so there is.
2. Say: There is a kitchen.
3. Two bedrooms, so there are.
4. Say: There are two bedrooms.
5. Join them with and, in one line.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not use it has for a room list.
It works, but there is sounds more natural here.
grammar.memoryTip: One room: is. More rooms: are.
grammar.practice:
Write is or are.
1. There ___ a kitchen.
2. There ___ three rooms.
3. There ___ no garden.
4. There ___ two windows.
5. There ___ a bathroom.
6. There ___ four beds.
grammar.answerKey:
1. is
2. are
3. is
4. are
5. is
6. are
Five or six right? Good.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Where do you live?
grammar.explanation: One question, and a short answer is enough.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Where do you live?
In a flat.
I live in a flat.

Do you live alone?
No, with my family.

Is it near here?
Yes, it is near the school.
grammar.workedExample:
Somebody asks where your home is.
1. A short answer is fine: In a flat.
2. A longer one: I live in a small flat.
3. They may ask: Alone?
4. Answer: No, with my family.
5. Two or three short lines is a real conversation.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say: Where you live?
English needs do in this question.
Yes: Where do you live?
grammar.practice:
Ask and answer.
1. Where do you live?
2. Do you live alone?
3. Is it near here?
4. How many rooms are there?
grammar.answerKey:
Any true answer is right.
Check: did you answer in a short sentence, not one word?
Did the question in 1 keep the word do?

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: My and our
grammar.explanation:
My is for you alone.
Our is for you and other people.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I live alone:        my flat, my kitchen
I live with people:  our flat, our kitchen

my  →  I
our →  we

This is my bedroom. That is our kitchen.
grammar.workedExample:
You share a flat with two people.
1. The flat belongs to all of you.
2. So use our: our flat.
3. But your bedroom is only yours.
4. So use my: my bedroom.
5. In one line: my bedroom in our flat.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not use our when you live alone.
It tells the listener something untrue.
grammar.memoryTip: My is one person. Our is more.
grammar.practice:
Write my or our.
1. I live alone. This is ___ flat.
2. We live together. This is ___ kitchen.
3. Only I sleep here. This is ___ bedroom.
4. We all use it. This is ___ bathroom.
5. I live with my family. This is ___ home.
grammar.answerKey:
1. my
2. our
3. my
4. our
5. our
Four or five right? Good.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Where I live
writing.promptAndInstructions:

It is on the second floor.

I live in is in the first one.

writing.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
writing.title: Writing 2 — One room
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Choose one room in your home.
Write four lines about it.
Say what there is, and where things are.
writing.modelText:
My bedroom is little.
There is a bed by the window.
There is a little table.
My bag is under the bed.
writing.successCriteria:
Four lines about one room.
There is or there are in two of them.
At least one line says where a thing is.
writing.extension: Add a line saying what there is NOT in the room.
